Owen: heads-up — small-seq p95 spiked ~2.8x on canary after driver 542.3 rolled at 03:10 UTC :eyes:
Owen: this is only for seq <= 32, large seqs fine. noticed throughput steady but latency tail bad
Maya: which canary pool? logs or perf dump?
Owen: canary-us-east-1-a (20% traffic). attaching quick perf dump and nvprof snippet:
Owen: ```
kernel pick: fast-vec-attn (was) -> scalar-fallback (now)
seq=16 avg=3.2ms p95=14.8ms (prev p95=5.2ms)
nvml: driver 542.3, cuda 12.2
```
Cihan: hmm autotuner tie-breaker probably moved threshold for small seqs after driver ability report changed. saw similar on h100 last month when tensor cores reported different occupancy stats
Maya: can you paste the autotune logs for the same run? the selector writes heuristics to /var/log/runtime/selector.log
Owen: pasted snippet:
Owen: ```
[selector] seq=16 candidate_scores: {vec_opt: 0.47, scalar_opt: 0.52}
[selector] tiebreak: prefer_lower_flops=true (changed)
[selector] chosen=scalar_opt
```
Sarah: that tiebreak flip looks suspect. why did we change prefer_lower_flops? I thought yesterday's micro-bench only touched long-seq heuristics
Cihan: QAed a patch that added a fallback for driver-reported warp occupancy variance, landed in runtime v0.42.3. It included prefer_lower_flops=true when driver reports unstable occupancy. Seems 542.3's occupancy jitter triggered it
Maya: can we reproduce locally by faking occupancy? run `./tools/run_autotune --force-occupancy=unstable --seq=16`
Owen: ran it — selector picks scalar path and perf matches canary spike
runtime-infra: deploy-bot triggered: "canary roll 542.3 -> 20% at 03:10 UTC"
Maya: mitigation options: 1) roll back driver on canary, 2) revert tiebreak heuristic, 3) add an override to prefer vec_opt for seq<=32 in selector config.
Cihan: agree. quickest low-risk is config override (3) and flush selector cache. if that fixes, promote to prod. fallback is driver rollback (1) but that's heavy.
Sarah: what's the test run for config override? 
Cihan: `./ci/perf_run --config=selector_override_smallseq.yaml --seq=16 --runs=50` gives p95 ~5.1ms in my local vm with mocked driver jitter
Owen: +1 on config override, then canary traffic ramp to 50% and watch p95 for 30m. if green, roll to prod. if still bad, schedule driver rollback window at 02:00 UTC tomorrow (ops oncall)
Maya: I'll author selector_override_smallseq.yaml and post PR. also add a short-lived metric alert: p95_smallseq > 1.8x baseline for 15m -> page oncall.
Sarah: please include a short blameless note in the rollback runbook about occupancy variance detection.
deploy-bot: created PR #4287 with selector_override_smallseq.yaml by Maya.
Owen: action items -> Maya: PR + metric alert; Cihan: build hotpatch to revert tiebreak if needed; Sarah: schedule rollback window if override fails. I'll monitor canary and post updates here. :thumbsup:
Maya: PR linked, running canary apply now (patch + selector cache flush).
Owen: canary p95 back to 5.3ms after override. ramping to 50% now. monitoring.
runtime-infra: note: logging enhanced for selector.debug until 04:00 UTC.
Cihan: if override holds, we'll prepare a small runtime patch to adjust tie-break defaults and add a driver-jitter detection signal to avoid future flip-flops.
Sarah: great — keep notes for postmortem. this thread will be the canonical record. :shipit:
Maya: thanks all, closing loop once prod is green.
